originalHeadingTexts: What gradients of philosophical thought can we assesses against particular philosophers?
For each of those gradients, provide at least 5 defined points.
I intend to populate those gradients with the names of philosophers who hold the views along the gradients. Provide advice on this next step.
originalPromptClassification: Three exact request prompts including original wording and typo.

responseDecisions.decision: Retained all nine subject areas and their three questions each. Distinguished comparison questions from ready-made linear scales; clarified how commitments can vary across works and issues rather than labeling an entire philosopher by one number.

Retained the original nine five-category groups and all 225 nested definition positions. Corrected conflations including Kant/external reality, James/verificationism, hylomorphism/monism, infinitism/foundationalism, pluralism/relativism, phenomenology/world denial, and fuzzy truth/probability. Explained noncanonical category names and comparison cases. Added nine explicitly editorial five-point scales inside this response because the taxonomy alone did not supply the requested defined gradient points. Defined each measured feature and disallowed treating absence of applicability as a midpoint.

Retained five research steps, twelve five-name example lists and five next steps. Corrected or flagged Berkeley as a dualism example, Leibniz’s plural monads, Kant’s mixed epistemology, Rorty, Confucius, Rawls and other boundary cases without silently dropping source positions. Added text/date/evidence requirements and distinguished provisional examples from settled placement on the new scales.

sourcesConsulted.label: Essays in Radical Empiricism, “A World of Pure Experience”

remainingConcerns: The original taxonomy has overlaps and nonstandard labels. Its category/list positions are intentionally preserved with corrections and caveats; the editorial supplement supplies the actual ordered scales.

Five-point scales are explicit teaching conventions, not equal intervals, exhaustive historical taxonomies or measurements of entire philosophers. The twelve name lists remain provisional examples requiring issue-specific primary-text placement.
The verifier reports listAndTableStructuresPreserved=false solely because an explicit response appendix adds nine lists. Every original list and all original item positions remain preserved.
